perspective:
From Vincent’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Vincent Chinana, a mechanic. Patrick Guzman is my long-time friend since our teens, a construction worker. We share blue-collar work and have collaborated using my mechanical skills and his construction expertise.

- At the diner, Patrick told me he is considering a new construction venture to expand his business. He said it seems like a good opportunity and worth the risk, but he is still weighing options. I told him I’d heard it was risky, worried about financial security, and suggested he reconsider or delay until he had more information. He thanked me and said he’d think it over more.

- Later, I noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At his construction site, I told him I felt he wasn’t telling me everything. He said it was complicated and he hadn’t wanted to worry me with details. I told him I felt betrayed as a friend by his lack of transparency. He apologized, said he should have been more open, and suggested sitting down to explain everything.

- In our detailed discussion at my garage, I learned the investment troubles were serious. Patrick told me he might lose a significant amount if it didn’t turn around soon. I offered to lend him money to cover short-term losses; he gratefully accepted.

- A month later at the coffee shop, I became aware of new information that the venture might actually turn a profit. I told Patrick this. He said it was starting to look up and that he was relieved we had stuck with it. I apologized for doubting him and proposed a joint venture; he agreed to work out the details.

- At my house, we were optimistic about the joint venture and met to draft a business plan. I said our combined skills could make it successful and that we should outline every step carefully. Patrick agreed and said we should cover all our bases and set it up for success.

I do not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts, unspoken reasons, or any events or information I did not observe or hear.
